question.problem:
Find the solution to the inequality $\frac{5t-6}{2}\le 1.$

The solution is $t$
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}.

current_example.worked_solution:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying both sides by $3{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2-5y}{3} & \le 4 \\ 3\cdot (\frac{2-5y}{3}) & \le 3\cdot 4 \\ \cancel{3}\cdot (\frac{2-5y}{\cancel{3}}) & \le 3\cdot 4 \\ 2-5y & \le 12\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles. 

Remember, when we divide an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}2-5y & \le 12 \\ 2-5y-2 & \le 12-2 \\ -5y & \le 10 \\ \frac{-5y}{-5} & \,\,\ge \,\,\frac{10}{-5} \\ y & \ge -2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y \ge -2.$
